, f. (not far in mg. from Skt. id., s.v. 5; but closer to Pali paṭipatti), behavior, practice, performance, esp. good behavior, religiously; opp. to vipratipatti, q.v.; here are included some passages previously misinterpreted (esp. those from): pratipatti (acc.) darśeti bahuprakāraṃ (v.l. ˚rāṃ) (vs), (the Buddha) shows (to men of various sorts) good behavior in many ways, or the various sorts of good behavior; pratipattyā ca saṃpādayet (prose), and (who) shall put into effect (this sūtra) by his behavior (conduct, in practice); ye tubhya dharma śrutvā pratipattim eṣyatī hi (vs), who, having heard the dharma from you, will arrive at proper behavior (i.e. will put it into practice); ˚ttīya saṃpanno, perfect in behavior; ārādhyate satpratipattimadbhir dharmo, by those having virtuous behavior; ˚tti-guṇasauṣṭhavāc ca, ˚tti-śobhayā 20; vācayā yatha vadanti te budhās tatra caiva pratipattiyā (in actual practice) sthitāḥ (vs); śrutvā ca tasmin pratipattiye sthito (vs), and having heard it he remains steadfast in it by his behavior; ˚ttiś ca mayāpi bhāṣitā iha sūtre (vs); pratipattitu, thru their holy behavior; sarvabodhisattvaśikṣā-pratipattayaḥ (Bhvr., characterized by practice of …); ˚ttiṣu vyādhinirghātanasaṃjñā, misquoted śatrunirghātana˚, to good behavior (should be applied) the name of destroyer of diseases; bhūtapratipattiḥ śramaṇaḥ, a monk of true (correct) behavior;; (see s.v. pratipanna); [Page364-b]; pratipatti-kāmo;; note esp. line 15, … anavakāśo yad ātmā vipratipattisthitaḥ parān samyak-pratipattau sthāpayet …, it is inconceivable that myself remaining in evil behavior should establish others in good behavior; pratipatti-vipratipattisthitānā(ṃ) sattvānām anutsargaḥ (not dismissing) ekāṃśavacanatā (speaking to them in the same way); (eteṣu …) dharmeṣu pratipattir na vipratipattiḥ, good, not bad, behavior; sarvatragāminī-pratipattijñāna-balam, see s.v. pratipad, which is here and often interchangeable with pratipatti. In read with ms. amuko bhikṣuḥ sa bhagavatā pratipa(t)tyeva vyākṛtaḥ (ed. ˚tāḥ, doubtless misprint): pratipattyā iva, as it seems by his intellectual realization (so Skt. pratipatti), or with confidence due to experience (so AMg. paḍivatti); the ed. em. to pratipadyeva, stating in note that Tib. reads sṅa nas, which means formerly and which I cannot relate to either reading. Is there a corruption?

, f., also ˚dā (= Pali paṭipadā), course of conduct, practice, behavior, esp. good, approved behavior, = pratipatti, q.v.; acc. to and, so also primarily Pali paṭipadā; this mg. is recognized by, which he reads by em. araṇya-˚daṃ samādāya (better, I think araṇāṃ pra˚, see s.v. araṇya; in that case render passionless way of behavior); he also accepts this mg. in puṇyāṃ pratipadam udbhāvayan dānadamasaṃyamādibhiḥ, displaying meritorious behavior by …; vākpragraheṇa pratipanmayena, by (the kind of) acceptance of his words which consists of behavior, i.e. by not only assenting verbally but putting them into practice; (anayāpi … caryayānayāpi) pratipadā (pratipad = caryā), and similarly; often rendered way, path, and called ‘a quasi-synonym of magga’ in; this is due to the fact that the middle course of conduct, madhyamā pratipad(ā), is (in BHS as in Pali) identified with the eight-fold way (mārga) stated in the fourth Noble Truth, but the terms are quite differently defined, ma˚ pra˚ being the course of behavior which steers between the two extremes (anta) of violent asceticism and worldliness; the lack of real synonymity between Pali magga and paṭipadā is shown, e.g., by (kaṅkhā vā vimati vā) Buddhe vā dhamme vā saṃghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā (obviously different things must be meant); madhyamayaiva pratipadā (contrasted with amadhyamā pratipad = violent asceticism,); here as elsewhere such a statement introduces the Four Noble Truths, the fourth of which is duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad (with or without āryasatyam, in without it, in 12 = eṣa evāryāṣṭāṅgamārgaḥ); so; (with āryasatyam) and 10 (without it); (without it); (with it); more metaphysical interpretations of the term madhyamā pratipad in; and repeatedly in following sections; one of the ten bala of a Tathāgata is sarvatragāmanī-pratipaj-jñānam, cf. sarvatragāminī-(the more usual form)-pratipatti-jñāna-balam (note obvious equivalence of pratipad and pratipatti!), power of knowledge of courses of conduct which may lead to any result; in same context sarvatragāminīṃ ca pratipadaṃ (v.l. ˚dāṃ) vetti (vs), and, for another, see s.v. pratipadā; parānukampā-pratipad, conducting oneself with compassion for others; nairyāṇika- (and ˚kī) pratipad, see s.v. nairyāṇika; śaikṣa-pratipady uttarikaraṇīyam (see this), in the course (practice; here we could also, no doubt, translate path) of the śaikṣa (q.v.); there are four courses of conduct (Tib. lam, way, path, but also manner of conduct), viz duḥkhā pra˚ dhandhābhijñā, sukhā pra˚ dhandhābhijñā, duḥkhā pra˚ kṣiprābhijñā, sukhā pra˚ kṣiprā˚ (for the corresponding Pali list, and interpretation, see s.v. paṭipadā). See also next.

(as in Pali paṭipadā), but very much rarer; hence, where saṃdhi is ambiguous, I have assigned the doubtful forms to pratipad: dharmadeśanāpratipadā-saṃpannaṃ … śāstāraṃ, perfected in the practice of preaching the law; ye sarvatragāminīpratipadāṃ tatratatragāminīpratipadāṃ … prajānanti, in list of the ten bala of a Tathāgata, see pratipad, towards the end; nirvāṇagāminī ˚dā; madhyamā ˚dā, between the two extremes, introducing Four Noble Truths; in 12 the word mārga is omitted, text reading yad idam āryāṣṭāṅgikā, sayyathīdaṃ samyagdṛṣṭiḥ etc.; but one ms. reads āryāṣṭāṅgikaḥ, implying mārgaḥ as in all known parallels, and the adaptation to the fem. gender of pratipad in one ms. (Pali paṭipajjati seems so used, but hardly Skt.; cf. pratipatti, ˚pad, ˚panna), behaves, with instr. of manner: yan nv aham alpāhāratayā pratipadyeyam (prose), suppose now I behave with (practise according to the method of) taking scant food. This seems the most probable interpretation; otherwise Tib., which renders the instr. -tayā by la, as if dative, and then has nan tan bya ḥo, I shall make earnest effort to eat scant food; I can hardly believe this is what the text means.

(or ˚srabdhi; = Pali paṭippassaddhi; to pratipraśrambha(ya)ti; cf. a-prati˚ and praśra˚), allaying, quieting, putting an end to: and, read ˚śrabdhyai for with all mss. ˚śraddhyai, unless semi-MIndic assimilation be assumed (Tib. rgyun chad; cpd. with sarvavedita-, sarveṣaṇa-, respectively); karmāvaraṇa-prati˚ (n. of a work); narakāpāya-pra˚; ˚dhaye, unto becoming peaceful;, see a-prati˚; sarvasattvakārya-prati˚, relaxation, abandonment of the interests of all beings (would ensue if Bodhisattvas entered nirvāṇa); ˚dhi-sukham, apparently sc. of obstacles, nivaraṇa; [Page366-a] cf. the next sentence; or possibly as in above, becoming peaceful?

, nt., also written ˚ṇa in mss. and some edd. (= Pali paṭi˚; usually considered a Buddhist word, see e.g., on, and s.v., where ‘late Skt.’ prati˚ is derived from Pali; yet Epic and Class. Skt. use at least the adj. pratibhānavant repeatedly, and see pratibhānavattvam, Geistesgegenwart; the difference is surely not great, but perhaps association with readiness in speech is more marked in Pali and BHS), presence of mind, self-confidence or brilliance, esp. as manifested in speech; quickwittedness, inspiration; Tib. spobs pa, courage, confidence; one of the four pratisaṃvid, q.v.; equivalent to commoner Skt. pratibhā, wit, presence of mind, whence niṣpratibhāna (,) is replaced in by niṣpratibha, in a cliché cited s.v. maṅku, q.v., where the mg. seems to be without presence of mind, abashed, out of countenance: (vs; the 3 other pratisaṃvid in 12, same vs); sarvabodhisattvadhāraṇī-pratibhāna-pratilabdhaiḥ; utkṛṣṭapra˚; jñānaparamā asaṃkliṣṭapratibhānāś ca; miscellaneous,; (one of ten vaśitā of bodhisattvas); (˚na-saṃpannāḥ, of bodhisattvas); anāchedya-pra˚ (of bodhisattvas); (tasya ˚nam utpannam, he became inspired to speak his thoughts); (spelled ˚ṇam, as often in mss. of, here kept in ed.); (anantaḥ ˚nena, of Tathāgatas);;;; (here the quality by which Avalokiteśvara ‘matures’, paripācayati, creatures);. See also pratibhānatā, -vant; asaṅga-prati˚.
= pratibhāna: (here by em. but quite certain), 9.
(= Pali paṭi˚; occurs in Skt.), possessing pratibhāna, q.v.:; (˚vantāś, mss. ˚vāṃś, n. pl.);; (vs; ˚vān, as n. pl.;).
, adj. (from ˚bhāna plus -ika): (nāpi ca) svayaṃpratibhāṇiko (grantho) (vs; so with one ms.), of oneʼs own invention or native wit; read ˚niko for ˚ṇiko (em. wrongly).
, error for ˚syate, fut. of Skt. pratibhāti, seems good: (na … rasatṛṣṇāvyavasitānām idaṃ praṇītaṃ) bhojanaṃ pratibhāsyate, this excellent food will not seem pleasing to …]

, m. (in this sense unrecorded elsewhere; also used as in Skt. in mgs. appearance,, presentation to the mind,), reflected image: (śakrasya … devānāṃ ca) ˚saḥ saṃdṛśyate sma (so Tib., gzugs brñan; possibly however only actual, literal appearance, as in Skt.); commonly as (mere) semblance, with emphasis on unreality, (kāmaguṇāḥ) … pratibhāsasamā naṭaraṅgasamāḥ.; māyā-marīci-svapnodakacandra-pratiśrutkā-pratibhāsa-;; in similar lists;;; (parallel with chāyā, svapna, pratiśrutkā); with things of [Page367-a] no value, tṛṇa-kāṣṭha-kuḍya-(adds vartma-)-pratibhāsopama; (here said of the body, as also in) and (ātma-pratibhāsavat, like an illusion, illusory image, of self); saṃsārasāgari anantān darśayase gatīyu (gen. sg.) ˚sān (vs), in the ocean of saṃsāra thou displayest endless semblances of (human) fate(s); in of toys, imitations of real things; in of the reflection of sun and moon in water.
, adj. (from ppp. of Skt. prati-bhid-, show up, reveal, plus -ka, perh. pejorative), shown up, betrayed, revealed: sa ˚kaḥ saṃlakṣayate (Index undecided?).
, m. (= Skt. pratibhū; M. paḍihua), surety, guarantor: pratibhuko (prose); (vss); elsewhere in the context pratibhū, e.g. ˚bhūr.
sg. fut., cf. Skt. pratibhū, I will warrant: (vs); no v.l.; meter correct; a nonce-form based on the noun;.

(in Pali only ppp. paṭimaṇḍita), adorns: perf. ˚ḍayām āsa; inf. ˚ḍayitum; ppp. ˚ḍita (various forms);;;;;;;;; (˚ḍikā, ed. em. ˚ḍitā);;;;;;. Cf. prec.

(in this sense not in Skt.; whether so used in Pali I am not sure; I have been unable to find the majority of references for paṭimāneti in), provides, presents with (instr., usually food): āhāreṇa pratimānetvā; ˚netha; ˚nito, ppp.,; (scilicet) a woman, (vs), mss. corrupt, perh. read: stryāgārāthiko iha gacche me pratimānaya, I came here wanting a woman; provide me (with one); daivatāni bhūtāni vṛṣṭyā ˚yanti (vs), the deities present creatures with rain. See also saṃpratimān˚.
, lit. ‘counter-seal’, seal impression: mudrāt pratimudra (a m.c.) dṛśyate (vs). Cited by also from, but not in Index to Kyoto ed. or.
(otherwise known only in caus. pratimohaya-in), becomes confused: na ˚hyema.

, ppp. (either to Skt. mokṣayati, denom., with prati, cf. Skt. pratimokṣaṇa; or ppp. to denom. from pratimokṣa, Pali paṭimokkha), ransomed, redeemed: (evaṃ Bhagavatā) sārthaś caurasahasrāt pratimokṣitaḥ.

, ppp. (to Skt. prati-yat-, not in this sense; Pali paṭiyatta), prepared, made: yehi iha advārakā gharā pratiyattā (mss. gharo pratipattā) bhavanti, by whom in this life doorless houses are prepared.
, begs, requests: sattvā āgatyābhayaṃ ˚cante sma (prose, no v.l.).
(nt.? in Skt. as ppp. only, not recorded otherwise; = Skt. pratirava), echo: (sarva-)ruta-pratirutaniścāraṇa-kauśalya-prāptatvād (prose, no v.l.).
, nt. (= Pali paṭi˚,, in closely similar vs), crying back, rejecting the ‘cry’ of one [Page367-b] who asks for something: yācanāṃ rodanam āhu adānam pratirodanaṃ (vs).
(Pali paṭirosati), is angry in return: roṣitaḥ ˚ṣayati; roṣito na ˚ṣayati;; roṣitena (˚tayā) na ˚roṣitavyam;.

, perfect observance (of the Law): saddharma-˚ṇa-tayā, by reason of the fact that he perfectly observes the Good Law; so Tib., dam paḥi chos yoṅs su sruṅ bas. No v.l., but em. to ˚rakṣaṇa (so,)? Or l for r, ? Prose; not in.

, adj. (also prāti˚, q.v.; to Skt. pratilambha plus -ika; cf. pratilābhika), suited (fit, ready) for attainment (of …; ifc.): (kāmāvacarāṇāṃ) devānām upapatti-pratilambhikam (see s.v. prāti˚) api tāvad divyaṃ cakṣuḥ, … suited to the birth (existence) of kāmāvacara gods (cf. upapatti); śamaikāyana-mārga- ˚kasya (sc. arhataḥ), (one) who is fit for getting …

, (app. to Skt. prati-lī-, Pali paṭilīyati, withdraws, turns back, and derivs.), should mean withdrawal (from), non-adherence (to): only in, said of bodhicittam, (sārathibhūtaṃ) mahāyāna-pratilayanapūrvaṃgamana-tayā; it seems probable that the true text was mahāyānāprati˚, with neg., it acts like a charioteer because of the fact that it is accompanied (conditioned, see pūrvaṃgamana) by not withdrawing (holding back) from the Great Vehicle.
, adj. (to Skt. pratilābha plus -ika; cf. pratilambhika), (what is) conducive to getting: dharmatā˚kam (Tib. rñed pa).
, adj. (to Skt. ˚lābha plus -in), getting, winning: tridaśādhipatyaṃ ˚bhino bhaviṣyanti; abstr. ˚bhi-tva, nt.: nirābhāsa-gocara-˚bhi-tvāt.

, adj. (ppp. to Skt. prati-lī-; not noted in this mg.), veiled: (read) navavadhūkā hi nāma pratilīnā tiṣṭhatīyaṃ punar vivṛtaiva sarvadā (wrong punctuation in, corrupt text in Calc. with apratilīnā, so recorded).

(var. ˚ṇaka), m., or ˚ṇikā (in mg. = Skt. pratirūpaka, which is also BHS; both = Tib. ltar bcos pa,), counterfeit, (false) imitation (of something, which usually precedes in comp.): prajñāpāramitā-˚ṇikaḥ (˚ṇakaḥ); the gender of the first element makes ˚ṇikā seem preferable, and this is used in the same cpd.; tasyāḥ (sc. prajnāpāramitāyāḥ) ˚ṇikām (in the foll. passage it is said to consist in the doctrine that impermanence, anityatā, of the skandhas means destruction, vināśa, of them); na (sc. prajñāpāramitā-)-prativarṇikāpi, not even the counterfeit (of it); bodhisattva-prativarṇikaḥ, a counterfeit bodhisattva. In several of these passages there are parallels with pratirūpa(ka). (See, for a different mg. in Skt.)

(ppp. of prati with denom. Skt. varṇayati), correspondingly (or, in return?) described or praised: buddhā deśenti vai yogaṃ mayā ca ˚tāḥ (vs), the Buddhas teach yoga, and are described (praised) by me accordingly (or, in return?).

, adj., obedient (to), subject to the will (of), with gen.: mama ˚śāś ca syuḥ, in a vs = Pali mam' evātivasā assu. The Pali ativasa is isolated, strange, and difficult (see), and BHS prativaśa seems a more natural and comprehensible form, tho also unparalleled as far as I know.

, nt., in Skt. (thing that is) equivalent (to something else): so Tib. (nor daṅ ḥdra ba) on; but in and Tib. (dṅos paḥi) skyin pa, [Page368-a] (personal) loan; here it seems to mean property left in trust, for safe-keeping, with another person. Cf. next.
, m. (to prec.), recipient of a fiduciary deposit:

, opposes, rejects (advice; a person), disobeys (a command, instruction); once ‘caus.’ prativāhayati in same mg.: ājñāṃ prativāhayāmi (prose); (ājñāṃ) prativahati; na mayā … bhagavataḥ … ājñā pratyūḍha-pūrveti (= ˚vā iti); vāṇīm a-prativahan (pres. pple.); (ye caināṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ) na pratikrośanti na prativahanti; (bodhisattva-piṭaka-)-prativahatānām aśrāddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ, of those disobeying (gen. pl. pres. pple.) …; prativahaty (so with mss., wrongly em.) eṣo 'smākam, he opposes (or rejects, repulses) us; evaṃ ca vyavacārayati na ca prativahati; te prativoḍhum ārabdhāḥ. See next.

, nt. (n. act. to prec.), opposition, rejection, disobedience: ˚nam = Tib. slar bzlog pa, turning back; (arthabhūtam) anartha-prativahana-tayā, it is of the nature of advantage, because it goes counter to disadvantages; dharmarājājñāprativahanatayā (i.e. ˚ājñā-aprati˚), because of not disobeying the commands of …

, f. (and ˚ṇi, nt.?; cf. a-prati˚, which see for Pali correspondents), opposition, repulsion, aversion to spoken words, especially to preaching or teaching; apparently a cpd. of prati and vāṇī: ˚ṇī, n. sg.,, and ˚ṇiḥ, id.,, both in reference to preaching or teaching; prativāṇi (? ˚ni without v.l., and Kyoto ed. suggests that their mss. read ˚ni, and that their ˚ṇi in text is an em.; cf. however aprativāṇi, where both edd. have ˚ṇi) = Tib. mi ḥphrod pa, unsuitable, disagreeable or the like; prob. of attitude towards teaching (the preceding entry is śaikṣābhir nikūjitaṃ). Form dubious; ending seems confirmed by aprativāṇi; n. sg. nt.? Or possibly adverb? In ˚vāṇi by em., rendered Opposition, which I think is about right.

, m., separate (and false) discrimination, making distinctions where fundamentally none exist; in seems interchangeable with parikalpa, etc., see, Glossary s.v. (where pratikalpa is also cited, but this is not in, and I have not noted it) and : bālaprativikalpam upādāya, etc. Cf. next.
(nt.) = prec.: vāg-akṣara-prativikalpanaṃ ca vinihatya; (anādikāla-prapañca-)dauṣṭhulya-sva-prativikalpanā, Bhvr., with bālapṛthagjanā(ḥ).

(denom. to ˚kalpa, q.v.), makes a (false) discrimination, discriminates (falsely): (na) lakṣaṇataḥ ˚payitavyāḥ, they are not to be (falsely) distinguished according to their (external) marks; dharmādharmaṃ ˚payanti; et alibi in.

(= Pali paṭi˚, so e.g.; see also saṃprativig˚), is dispersed, becomes scattered, vanishes: sā (dṛṣṭiḥ, wrong opinion) ˚vigatā; ˚gataḥ (madya-madaḥ? uncertain); (rūpa-madaḥ); (aiśvarya-madaḥ), 11 (bala-madaḥ); (sattveṣv āghātaḥ); abhūtvā bhavati bhūtvā ca prativigacchati; (yo dohadaḥ sa) ˚gataḥ.

, f. (to prec.), (separate, specific) recognition:, in definition of vijñāna as vastuprativijñaptir; (? reading uncertain); (but in 7 replaced by vijñaptiḥ; see s.vv. ādhipateya, ārambaṇa 3).

(= Pali paṭivijjhati), penetrates; [Page368-b] physically, aṅgāni ˚yanti (passive!) (prose), are penetrated; = reaches, attains (a place): ˚yate padaṃ śāntaṃ, reaches the peaceful place (same vs in Pali adhigacche); usually fig., penetrates intellectually, understands: ˚yati (dharmān); (prajñayā); (arthaṃ); (tathāgataviṣayaṃ); (parallel with vyavacārayati, q.v., and other synonyms); ˚yate (arthaṃ); na kiṃcin na ˚yati, does not fail to comprehend anything; ˚yan (pres. pple.); ˚ya (ger.); (arthaṃ); ˚viddha, ppp., dharmasvabhāva- ˚ddha-cittāḥ (Bhvr.); su-pratividdha, (dharmo … bodhisattvena …); (śūnyatā samyakprajñayā);. See next.
(nt.; to prec. plus -ana; Pali a-ppaṭivijjhana), comprehension: aśarīrasarvadharmanaya-˚natayā (instr. of -tā).
, m. (= Pali paṭi˚; cf. prativinīta), removal, suppression: pipāsā-˚vinayo (same phrase in Pali has pipāsa-vinayo).
, abandons:; so also; acc. to, error for prativiniḥsṛjati, and = pratiniḥ˚, q.v. (pratinisṛjati precedes this in).
(ppp. of ˚nayati = Pali paṭivineti, ˚nīta; cf. a-prati˚, prativinaya), removed: ˚tā, of kāmādhyavasānā and the like.

(rare), usually ˚nodayati (= Pali paṭivinodeti), dispels, removes, gets rid of: simplex only in prativinudanti (rajaḥ) in vs = 25 = (perh. m.c.?); otherwise only ˚nodayati, as in Pali: mārgaśramaṃ ˚nodya (ger.);;;;;; ˚dayeyam (daurmanasyaṃ);; ˚dayati (duḥkhaṃ); (ālasyakausīdyān); ˚dayituṃ (kāṅkṣāyitatvaṃ, q.v.); object, (the effects of) sin: ˚nodituṃ (kaukṛtyaṃ); ˚dayāmi, etc. (vadhaṃ); ˚dayitu-kāmaḥ (āghātaṃ). See next.

, nt. (to ˚nodayati, see prec., plus ana; = Pali paṭivi˚), removal, dispelling, getting rid of: (kaukṛtyasya, i.e. of the effects of sin); (nidrāklama-); (saṃśayānāṃ); (śoka-kaukṛtya-); (tad-, sc. āpatti-).
, perceives distinctly: evaṃ vidarśanayā prativipaśyataḥ (gen. sg. pres. pple.); ˚śyati; ˚śyan 15.

, dishonoring: kalyāṇadharma-˚nā (prose). No cpd. prati-vi-man-seems to be recorded.

, ppp., adj. (to ˚ramati; = Pali paṭi˚, also a-ppaṭi˚), abstained, ceased, usually with abl., or preceding stem in comp., of sin abstained from: (prāṇātipātāt);; (prāṇātipāta-prati˚);, read as one cpd. sarvākuśalakriyāprativiratā(ḥ), and delete punctuation before and after; (prāṇātipātāto, etc.);;; a-prati˚.
, f. (= Pali paṭi˚; cf. prec. and next), abstention (from sin):, in cpds., precisely parallel to virati; (prāṇātipātāt);;;.
(nt.; to next plus -ana), = prec.:; Cf. also prativairamaṇa.
(= Pali paṭi˚, cf. prec. three items), abstains (from sin): ˚ramāmi (vs; akhilavacanāt; mss. ˚viremi, em.);;;; ˚ramanti; fut. ˚ramiṣyaṃ (1 sg.) (prāṇātipātāt, etc.); ˚raṃsyanti;.
, ppp. to unrecorded prati-vi-rah- (cf. Skt. virahita), let go, given up, abandoned: su-˚hitāḥ (sarvopakaraṇakośā … vividhopakaraṇavidhayaḥ).

, ppp. (= Pali paṭi˚; see next), hostile, at odds (with, instr. with saha): uttarapañcālarājo dakṣiṇapañcālarājena saha ˚ddho babhūva; tāv anyonyaṃ ˚ddhau babhūvatuḥ; (tasya rājño vijite 'nyatamaḥ kārvaṭikaḥ) ˚ddhaḥ (wrongly rendered rebellious in Index and).
(m.; = Pali paṭi˚; like prec. to Pali paṭivirujjhati, which would be BHS prativirudhyate, ˚ti, but has not been recorded), hostility: ˚dha- (in comp.).
(cpd. of vilomayati, q.v.), opposes, goes against: bhāṣitaṃ ˚mayanti.
, adj. or subst. (to compv. of Skt. ˚śiṣṭa; specifying -ka?), (one that is) more (especially) distinguished: bodhisattvaḥ vṛddhatarakaṃ guṇa-prati˚kaṃ dṛṣṭvā samyak saṃbhāṣayaty ….

, nt. (cf. id. cited as adj. from, ein Gegengift enthaltend, and ˚ṣā, ibid., a kind of aconite, in medical texts), antidote for poison: acc. to Tib. (boṅ ṅa dmar po; there is an alternative gloss, ḥab śan tse ḥu, which I cannot interpret) on, red wolfsbane (aconite); prativiṣa-bhūtaṃ (sc. bodhicittaṃ) karma (2d ed. kāma-)-rativiṣanirviṣīkaraṇatayā.

(caus. of prati with veṭhayati, not recorded in Pali or Pkt., while Skt. prati-veṣṭ-is not recorded in this mg.), causes to be enveloped: puṣkariṇīṃ pratisīrāhi (q.v.) ˚ṭhāpehi (em., but sound; cf. line 15 pratisīrāhi veṭhāpitā).

, m. (= Pali paṭi˚; to Skt. prati-vyadh-, cf. Skt. vedha), (intellectual) penetration (only in this fig. mg.): (dharma-pra˚); (-satyanaya-pra˚); (prativedha-parākramāḥ, mss. ˚vikramāḥ, unmetr., possessing heroism of penetration); (buddhadharma-pra˚); (atyantājarāmaraṇadhātu-pra˚); (dharmadhātu-prativedha-jñāna-);;;; duṣ-pra˚ hard to penetrate (= Pali duppaṭi˚), (of saṃskāra); (of yogins).
, f. ˚ikā (= Skt. ˚veśa), neighbor: avidhāvidhaṃ prativeśikā(ḥ) (vs; so read with 1 ms.; em.), O neighbors (fem.)!
, adj. or subst. m. (cf. Skt. vaikārika, from vikāra), ˚kāḥ, ‘counter-disturbing(-elements)’, people who cause dissension and trouble:, in uddāna vs, referring, it seems, to, quarrelsome monks.
, nt. (= prativiramaṇa and vairamaṇa; blend of these two?), abstention: prāṇātipāta-pra˚ (prose).

, f. ˚ā, adj., true to vows (of chastity): ˚tānāṃ, applied to female ascetics (tāpasīnāṃ 5); v.l. both times pati˚, which could not apply here in its normal mg. true to oneʼs husband (so also Pali patibbatā); AMg. paivvayā is glossed prativratā, and rendered thus in both Guj. and Hindi, yet the Skt. gloss is patiṃ vratayati (); for Skt. prati AMg. usually has paḍi, rarely pai. For pativratā a v.l. prati˚ is recorded; but there is no such v.l. in, and Tib. says clearly not unfaithful to her husband. Possibly MIndic forms of Skt. pativratā came to mean simply chaste, and then [Page369-b] became applicable even to female ascetics; the form prati˚ might then be an unhistorical hyper-Sktism.
(treated as nt.; for Skt. pratiśraya, m.; semi-MIndic), lodging: so … anyasmiṃ grāme vāsopagato, anyatarāye vṛddhāye pratiśayaṃ dinnaṃ.
, often written for pratisaraṇa, q.v.; no distinction of mg. between the spellings.
, m. (to next), one who stores up, collects (creatures, gen., as if treasures; said of a bodhisattva): (sarveṣām eva … sattvānām …) samyak-pratiśāmakaś ca.

, also ˚śam˚ and erroneously ˚śrām˚, ˚sam˚ (= Pali paṭisāmeti, puts away, stores; wrongly), (1) stores away (property): hiraṇya (so read) … (etc.) ˚śāmayet (so Nep. mss., with ˚yīt) (vs); bhāṇḍaṃ ˚śāmitaṃ (mss. ˚śrām˚); bhāṇḍaṃ ˚śāmayanti (subject merchants); bhāṇḍaṃ ˚śāmya (subject a housewife); (2) puts away (a monkʼs bowl and robe, after his begging-round): pātracīvaraṃ ˚śāmayitvā; ˚śrāmya, ed. with mss., read ˚śāmya,; ˚śāmya;; (a monkʼs bed, or bed and seat, preparatory to setting out on a journey, on which he takes bowl and robe with him), (paribhuktaṃ) śayanaṃ pratiśāmya; yathāparibhuktaṃ śayanāsanaṃ pratiśamayya;; written ˚samayya, pātracīvaraṃ pra˚;;;; yathāparibhukta-śayanāsanaṃ pra˚; (3) harbors (a person), entertains (privately): (surakṣitaḥ kartavya iti.sa) tena pratiśāmitaḥ; (ye āgantukā bhikṣavo …) tān asau pratiśāmya ib.; others, etc. See also pratisamarpayati.

, in śiṣya-pra˚, perhaps (pupilʼs) pupilhood: (yasya tāvad) vayaṃ śiṣya-pratiśiṣyakayāpi na tulyāḥ, of whom (viz. the Buddha), you see, we are not equal to the pupilʼs pupilhood (having been shown to be inferior to Cunda, the novice-attendant of Śāriputra, the disciple of Buddha). Index and) means substantially cure, orig. however clearly (required) means (of treatment); note that pratyaya in BHS is not used as equivalent of pariṣkāra in this sense, as Pali paccaya is alleged to be used by both and; bhojana-gilānapraccayaṃ (semi-MIndic) (vs); (3) pratyayabuddha, one who becomes a Buddha by (understanding of) causes, = a pratyeka-buddha, q.v.: (vs), [Page376-a] where a marginal gloss has pratyekabuddha (which would be unmetr.); so also pratyaya-jina; and pratyaya-yāna = pratyeka-(buddha-)yāna (vs; follows śrāvakayāna, and followed by uttama-yāna = mahāyāna; misunderstood by); the same mg. is expressed by pratyayair jinā(ḥ) (vs; refers to pratyekabuddhas, mentioned two lines before); the application of the term is made clear by a passage in, where first,, we read: tatra kecit sattvāḥ paraghoṣaśravānugamanam ākāṅkṣamāṇā ātmaparinirvāṇahetoś caturāryasatyānubodhāya tathāgataśāsane 'bhiyujyante, ta ucyante śrāvakayānam ākāṅkṣamāṇās … (the hīnayāna followers); then,, anye sattvā anācāryakaṃ jñānaṃ damaśamatham ākāṅkṣamāṇā ātmaparinirvāṇahetor hetu-pratyayānubodhāya tathāgataśāsane 'bhiyujyante, ta ucyante pratyekabuddhayānam ākāṅkṣamāṇās …; and finally,, apare punaḥ sattvāḥ sarvajñajñānaṃ … ākāṅkṣamāṇā … sarvasattvaparinirvāṇahetos tathāgatajñānabalavaiśāradyānubodhāya tathāgataśāsane 'bhiyujyante, ta ucyante mahāyānam ākāṅkṣamāṇās …; here it is very clearly characteristic of pratyekabuddhas that they seek to understand (anubodhāya) grounds and reasons, whereas śrāvakas seek to understand only the four noble truths, and mahāyānists seek to understand the whole knowledge, etc., of Tathāgatas. The śrāvakas are also said to be content with following what they hear said by others (i.e. of the gospel); pratyekabuddhas go deeper, but not so deep as mahāyānists. In pratyaya-pravāraṇāyā (see pravāraṇā) is, in a v.l., read pratyeka-prav˚, which seems to have been the reading used by Chin. (secrète); the Pali parallel, however,, has cātumāsapaccaya-pavāraṇā, and the old comm.,, understands paccaya = gilāna-paccaya, i.e. our 2 above; it may be that some confusion has occurred in the tradition; did the redactor, reading pratyaya-, have in mind both the above-mentioned use of pratyaya-buddha for pratyeka-b˚, and at the same time the curious use of pratyeka described under that word (and did he even substitute pratyaya for it)?

(AMg. paccoyarai, see), descends, disembarks: vahanāt (from a ship) ˚tarasva.
, addresses, calls to (from a distance, in the places recorded): (sa tair dūrata eva dṛṣṭaḥ.) te taṃ ˚ṣitum ārabdhāḥ; (sā taṃ dūrata) eva ˚ṣitum ārabdhā.
, departs, withdraws, steps back: ppp. ˚sṛteṣu bhikṣubhikṣuṇīṣu, when … had departed; ger. ˚sṛtya, having stepped back, withdrawn.

, adj. (cf. next; to prec.), belonging to oneself: ˚kaṃ dhanam, wealth that is my own.

, f. ˚kī, adj., found in Skt., peculiar, pertaining to the individual; private, personal, contrasting with general, universal: ˚kaṃ jñānabalaṃ mamaitat (vs), this is my (Buddhaʼs) peculiar power of knowledge; Buddha saves all men by the Buddha-(= mahā-)yāna alone, and does not preach individual (personal, private) release for any creature, i.e. by the śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha ways, na ca kasyacit sattvasya ˚mikaṃ parinirvāṇaṃ vadati (prose); similarly, ˚mikīṃ nirvṛti kalpayāma … na bhūyaḥ (vs); in this light interpret (vs) ete 'pi śraddhāya mamaiva yānti, ˚mikaṃ jñānu na caiva vidyate, they too walk in (by?) faith in me alone, and there is no individual (private) knowledge at all found in them, which would lead to their seeking selfish, individual nirvāṇa; and see a contrast between the two halves of the line, which seems unjustified.)
, m. (cf. Skt. ādeśa), with lābha, substitute, surrogate (munificence, to monks):; defined as one made at all, or only one, of the four mahācaitya, q.v.

= prec., acc. to, cited from; not in or Kyoto ed., but for [Page377-b], see under prec., cites this as a v.l.; is this the source of, cited by ?]

, m. (also as misreading or var. for pravyā˚, q.v.), in one of five ‘foods’; otherwise only four are listed in BHS and Pali, see s.v. kavalīkārāhāra; this seems to be an addition and its mg. is not clear; the list is otherwise questionable.

(to praty-ud- with Skt. har-, not used in this sense in Skt.; Pali paccuddharati is usually [Page378-a] wrongly interpreted; it means removes [water, or coloring, with a cloth], and; see also next items; the range of mg. in Pali and BHS, for the whole group, is something like remove, take away, take back, withhold, restrain), holds back, restrains, moderates: ˚dhareti or ˚dharesi, to be read for mss. ˚dharehi (em. ˚dhāreti),, see s.v. samajya. , m. (to praty-ud-dharati, q.v., but in somewhat different mg.; cf. next), the act of taking back (approval, or a gift, once given): chanda-˚raḥ = Tib. dad pa phyir bsgyur ba (approving, then later changing); so Jap., which understands the monkish rules of discipline as the object; Chin. first showing respect for another (person, or possibly thing) then going back on it; changing oneʼs mind; so interpret pratyuddhāra-tām avabhāsa-tāṃ (q.v.) ca pratilabdhukāmena, by one who (wrongfully) seeks to take back (prob. a gift he has promised, see next) …

The old,, makes my interpretation unmistakably clear; note especially 24 paccuddhārake paccuddhārakasaññī, anāpatti, there is no offense in the case of a thing that may (properly) be resumed, when (the one who so acts) knows that it is; cf. 17—18 which explains the circumstances under which it is apaccuddhāraka (implying that it is paccud˚ in other cases).

, nt. , ppp. (to Skt. praty-upa-sthā-; cf. Sudeṣṇāṃ pratyupasthāsye Cr. ed., I shall wait on Sudeṣṇā), (1) waiting upon, often foll. by a form of bhū, waits upon (with gen. of person, instr. of thing): buddhakṛtyena sattvānaṃ ˚to 'bhūt, (Pūrṇa) waited upon creatures with Buddha-service; buddhakṛtyena ca ˚taḥ (no person, no form of bhū) (vs); (rājā …) samyaksaṃbuddhasya … sarveṇa ˚to abhūṣi ( om. abhūṣi);, waited upon the Enlightened One with everything (which he needed); (tasyāṃ) dharmadeśanāyāṃ ˚tā bhavāmaḥ, we are in attendance (on the Buddha) at this preaching of the Law; prob. also tvam evaṃrūpayā sattvārthakriyayā ˚sthitā, you wait on (creatures) with such activity advantageous to creatures (but possibly passive, as in next passage); with passive force, pañcasu sthāneṣu ˚tau (mātāpitarau), waited upon in five matters (by their son); (2) concerned in (a specialization of the meaning present, on hand, Skt. and BHS), with loc. and instr.: (na hy ākāśadhātur) gamane vā āgamane vā ˚taḥ, na strībhāvena na puruṣabhāvena ˚taḥ, for the space-element is not concerned in going or coming, nor in femininity or masculinity (with instr., perh. lit. attended by?).

(nt.; no cpd. of ās- with praty-upa- is recorded anywhere; one might think of em. to paryupā˚, q.v., but in Pkt. this appears as AMg. etc. pajjuvāsa-, whereas pratyup˚ would give *paccuv˚; hence such an em. could not easily be based on the Pkt. confusion of paḍi-with pari-,), service, waiting upon: ˚na-vaineyānām.
, f. ˚ikā (= Skt. pratyupta, ppp.; the suffix ka may be specifying in, but apparently not in), set (with jewels), studded; see s.v. āmukta.

, adj., chiefly as prior member of cpds. (but cf. pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ;; ˚kāyāṃ bodhau;; ˚kā bodhiḥ), primarily as in Skt., for a single person, individual, personal; esp. common in pratyekabuddha and other cpds. showing this mg., see the foll. items; in some BHS cpds., in part with equivalents in Pali, this seems to have developed special connotations, possibly owing to the standard contrast between a pratyekabuddhaʼs rating (far inferior) and that of a real (samyak-saṃ-)buddha. So pratyekaniraya (Pali pacceka-n˚) or ˚naraka seems clearly to be a place of less severe punishment than a (mahā-, or regular) niraya: note (yadi kecit, sc. bodhisattvāḥ, kathaṃcid … avīciṃ mahānirayaṃ gacchanti, atha khalu) pratyekanirayaṃ gacchanti (text adds, they are never born as pretas, asuras, etc.); also; pratyekanarakaḥ = Tib. ñi tshe baḥi (ephemeral; single, simple,; adds, very small, minute; animals that do not live more than a day) sems can (creatures) dmyal ba (hell), app. then a hell in which creatures live for a short time; Chin. individual hell; no Jap. rendering; iha pratyekanarakeṣūpapannāḥ … asmābhir itaś cyutair narakeṣūpapattavyaṃ bhaviṣyati (app. for further, more serious punishment); bahuśaṅkur nāma pratyekanarakaḥ; śramaṇavarṇapratirūpakaṃ nāma pra˚narakaṃ (n. sg.!); ˚narakān; ˚narakaḥ; (tasminn eva janmani) pratyekasvargaṃ pra˚narakaṃ (n. sg.) cānubhūtam (refers to story of which is part); here private, personal heaven and hell seem to fit, since the one who experiences both seems to be a single individual (at a given time; a former inhabitant of the pra˚naraka is released as the new one arrives); pratyeka-rājan (see s.v. pṛthu), contrasting with cakravartin, either minor, subordinate, or individual (belonging to a single land?); [Page379-a] pratyeka-brahman (= Pali pacceka˚, an independent Brahma),, see s.v. Baka (, devenu un des Brahmas, which can hardly suffice); in, most strangely, the words brāhmaṇa and pratyeka-brā˚ seem used for (the god) Brahman and pratyeka-brahman: (bodhisattvā avaivartikadharmā … never enter an evil existence,) atha khalu brāhmaṇā bhavanti pratyekabrāhmaṇā vā indrāś ca upendrāś ca yakṣādhipatayaś ca yakṣāś ca … (note parallelism between pratyeka-br˚, contrasting with br˚, and upendra and yakṣa, contrasting with Indra and yakṣādhipati).
(m. or nt.), -niraya, see pratyeka.

in a number of passages pra˚ is bracketed or closely associated with vikalpa, and the contexts suggest vain fancy, false imagining: viṣayavikalpahetukam anādikāla-prapañca-vāsanāhetukaṃ ca, and similarly; tasya savastukasya vikalpasya nirodho yaḥ, sa sarva-prapañca-nirodho veditavyaḥ; evaṃ ca prapañca-nirodho (etc., as cited s.v. parinirvāṇa); saṃjñāvikalpāḥ prapañca-saṅgānugatā(ḥ); sarva-vikalpa-prapañcātītā(ḥ) (tathāgatāḥ); jalpa-prapañcābhiratā hi bālās, see jalpa, the interpretation of which is doubtful, which increases the uncertainty of prapañca; prapañcārāma-, delight in pra˚; ˚cārāmam adhikṛtyāha. followed by a series of vss on the subject (prapañca-cārin, acting with or according to …); pra˚ bracketed with vigraha, strife,; its object is possessions, 4—7 (na vo 'sti kṣetraṃ na kṛṣir vaṇijyā syur yasya arthāya prapañca etc 6—7); next a vs devoted to vigraha, as based on family and possessions, 8—11; then again a vs on pra˚, ending prapañca varjitva janetha kṣāntim 15; prapañca-cāra, the course of pra˚, again contrasted with kṣānti, 18—19; parallel with iñjana, manyana, spandana (text syan˚), (vs), see prapañcana and ˚cita, similarly used; important is, (prakṛti-)śānte niḥsvabhāve tathāgate sarvaprapañcātīte mandabuddhitayā śāśvatāśāśvatādikayā nityānityāstināstiśūnyāśūnyasarvajñāsarvajñādikayā (here a kārikā vs:) prapañcayanti (see this) ye buddhaṃ prapañcātītam avyayaṃ, te prapañca-hatāḥ sarve na paśyanti tathāgataṃ. (Comm. continues:) vastu-nibandhanā hi prapañcāḥ syur, avastukaḥ (so!) ca tathāgataḥ, kutaḥ prapañcānāṃ pravṛttisaṃbhava iti.ataḥ prapañcātītas tathāgataḥ … tam itthaṃvidhaṃ tathāgataṃ svotprekṣitamithyā-parikalpamala-malina-mānasa-tayā vividhair abhūtaiḥ parikalpaviśeṣair ye buddhaṃ bhagavantam prapañcayanti, te svakair eva prapañcair hatāḥ santas …; here false fancy, vain imagining, seems not far wrong; note parikalpa associated with it; prapañcopaśamaḥ (vs), with sarvopalambhopaśamaḥ.
